4. The plaintiff case in short, is that Jozeshwar Sharma, Rajeshwar Sharma, Ratneshwar Sharma and Guneshwar Sharma were the CS recorder owners of 1.78 acres of land in CS Khatian No. 252, CS Plot Nos. 502, 503 and 504; that each of them was owner of 4 annas share in the land, while on the basis of amicable settlement, they have been possessing the respective portion of their land, Guneshwar Sharma died issueless leaving behind wife Kusum Kumari Debi as his successor and during SA survey her name was duly recorded in SA Khatian No. 307 in 4 annas share with other co-sharer and had been possessing the same for more than statutory period of limitation; that while she was in possessing of the said land due to her legal necessity, she transferred 0.1650 acres of land in plot No. 504, 0.1250 acres in plot No. 503 and 0.1500 acres in plot No. 502 in total = 0.4450 acres of land to Hajee Al-Helal Uddin by sale-deed No. 7115 dated 23-7-1969; that against the aforesaid sale, the SA recorded owner Hossain Uddin filed Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No. 12 of 1970 in the First Court of Sub-ordinate Judge, Dhaka and the said case was allowed in favour of Hossain Uddin by judgment dated 7-1-1978; that thereafter Hossain Uddin transferred 0.2950 acres in favour of Hajee Haider Ali by two sale-deeds being Nos. 805 and 850 both dated 7-1-1978; that out of total area 0.4450 acres, Hajee Haider Ali transferred 4 kathas of land out of plot Nos. 502 and 503 to Md Ibrahim and Julekha Begum vide four sale-deeds being Nos. 8403, 8404, 8405 and 8406 all dated 8-3-1979 and delivered possession; that Md Ibrahim and Julekha Begum then transferred 2(two) kathas of land and remained in possession over the rest 2(two) kathas of land by constructing semi-pucca building and had been in possession of the said property through tenants; that subsequently they executed a registered power-of-attorney No. 11925 dated 3-8-1997 and appointed Md Haider Ali as their constituted attorney; that thereafter constituted attorney Haider Ali transferred 2(two) kathas of land in favour of the plaintiffs by sale-deed No. 3649 dated 11-3-1998; that plaintiffs then by determining specific boundary of the property mutated their names and after obtaining necessary permission and approval of plan from RAJUK constructed 4-storied building thereon and have been paying all sort of rents and taxes to the respective authority. 

 24. It appears from the sale-deed No. 7115 dated 23-7-1969 (Exhibit-1) that by the said sale-deed Haji Helal Uddin got this property from Kusum Kumari Devi wife of Guneshwar Sharma. Since Hossain Uddin being a co-sharer of the land, he filed a pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No. 12 of 1970 case (Exhibit-2) and same was allowed. Thereafter, Hossain Uddin transfered 29.50 decimals of land to Haji Haider Ali by two deeds being Nos. 805 and 850 both dated 7-1-1978 (Exhibit-3 and 3-ka). Subsequently, Haji Haider Ali transferred 4(four) kathas of land of Plot Nos. 502 and 503 to Ibrahim and Julekha Begum vide two registered sale-deeds being Nos. 8405 (Exhibit- 5) and 8406 (Exhibit-4) both dated 8-3-1979 and delivered possession. Thereafter Md Ibrahim and Julekha Begum transferred 2(two) kathas of land and remained in possession over rest 2(two) kathas of land by constructing four-storied building. Present plaintiffs claimed title of the property by way of purchase from Md Ibrahim and Julekah Begum through kabala No. 3649 dated 11-3-1998 (Exhibit-7). After purchase they mutated their names in the khatians (Exhibit-8- 8(kha) and obtaining permission/sanction from the Rajuk by sanction letter dated 9-12-1999 (Exhibit-9-9(kha) and constructed four-storied building on the suit land. Since then they have been in continuous possession, which was clearly found by the trial Court. 

 26. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, the decisions cited and the provisions of Hindu law in respect of Hindu widow claiming interest in the property, we are of the opinion that the trial Court totally miss-appreciated and misconstrued the judgment and sole decree passed in Title Suit No. 368 of 2001 (Exhibit-14 series). Although the trial Court upon consideration of the Exhibits of the plaintiffs rightly found that the plaintiffs are in possession of the suit land by constructing four-storied building with the sanction and approved plan passed by Rajuk and mutated their names in the khatian and by paying rents and taxes to the respective authorities but erroneously dismissed the suit.
